To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have discovered two massive clusters at z ≈ 1, that they are morphologically and thermally similar to nearby clusters, and that they are consistent with a non-evolving M-T relation.

(1) we present a study of the high-redshift clusters Cl J1113-2615 and ClJ0152-1357, (2) we find the first cluster at z ≈ 1.0 to have a mass similar to the Coma Cluster and (3) we find no significant evolution of the cluster scaling relations from z = 0 to z ≈ 1.
the X-ray properties of the high-redshift clusters Cl J1113-2615 and ClJ0152-1357 do not evolve significantly from those of nearby systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of massive clusters of galaxies.
the evolution of the properties of the intracluster gas, which is a tracer of the assembly history of massive galaxy clusters, in the context of the hierarchical growth of structure.
the evolution of the intracluster medium (ICM) and the cluster M-T and L-T relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at z ≈0.8, the clusters are consistent with having been assembled at z ≳ 0.8.
the properties of massive high-redshift clusters are consistent with the predictions of the low-ΩM cosmological models.
the cluster properties appear to have been in place at high redshifts, but that the data are not yet sufficient to rule out a more complex picture in which some of these properties have evolved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two clusters are massive and hot and that the X-ray data are consistent with the clusters being assembled at redshift z > 0.8.
the properties of massive galaxy clusters at z ≈ 1 do not appear to have changed significantly from those at the present day.
, in the absence of a significant evolution in the cluster properties at z ≈ 1, the high redshift of Cl J0152-1357 is likely due to the fact that the subclusters have not yet merged.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of massive clusters are not significantly different at z ≈ 1 than they are at z ≈ 3.
, at z ≈0.8, the properties of massive clusters of galaxies are consistent with those found for nearby clusters.

, while we have found no evidence of evolution in the cluster M-T, L-T, gas fraction-T, or metallicity-T relations, the cluster masses are significantly smaller than predicted from local relations, indicating that clusters are assembled at significantly higher redshifts than z ≈ 0, in agreement with low-ΩM cosmologies.
